input.question: What was popular British opinion of the American Revolution?
input.ground_truth: Something that could be used to gauge popular opinion in that time was voting in the House of Commons. The last time any PM was defeated over issue of war and peace (until David Cameron on Syria) was in 1782 regarding the rebellious American colonies.

response.prediction:
Okay! Let’s imagine you have a big family, and some of your cousins live far away. One day, your cousins decide they don’t want to follow the rules your whole family has been using anymore. They want to make their own rules.

Now, some of your other relatives (let’s say, your British uncles and aunts) don’t like this idea. They think your cousins should just stay and follow the family rules. But some of your cousins’ friends (and maybe a few of your aunts and uncles) think it’s a good idea for your cousins to try making their own rules.

So, when it comes to the American Revolution, "popular British opinion" means what most people in Britain thought about the American colonies wanting to be their own country.

Most British people, especially those in charge, didn’t like the idea. They thought the colonies should stay part of Britain and follow the king’s rules. But some people in Britain thought the colonies should be allowed to have their own rules, though not that many.

So, most British people did **not** like the American Revolution—they wanted the colonies to stay with Britain. But a few people thought it was okay for the colonies to try something new.
